title: Showcase: the machine that lifts
summary: Combine the lever, the gear train and what was learned about friction into one rig that lifts a real load for the family, with the numbers on a card.
materials: the lever, gears and spring scale from weeks 1 to 3
a real load to lift (a small bag, a book, a toy)
the Maker's Log, open to weeks 1 to 3

steps.title: Build the rig and plan the demo
steps.body:
Pick one real load heavier than anything lifted so far this sprint, and build a rig from the lever or the gear train, or both together, that can lift it. Aim it at something a lever or a gear train genuinely helps with: a load too heavy to lift comfortably by hand alone.

Plan the demo in this order.

1. Show the load and say roughly how much force it would take to lift it straight up, from week 1's numbers.

2. Show the rig and say which trade it uses: a longer effort arm, a gear ratio, or both.

3. Lift the load with the rig in front of the family.

4. Read the actual force off the spring scale as it lifts, and say how it compares with lifting it by hand.

Write the two numbers, straight lift and rig lift, big on an index card to hold up during the demo.

figure.alt: The rig, built from the lever or gear train or both, lifts the load while the spring scale is pulled to read the actual lifting force. An index card nearby holds the two numbers to compare: the straight lift-by-hand force and the rig's force.

steps.title: Rehearse the lift
steps.body:
Run the whole lift twice before the family sees it: once slowly, checking every part holds, and once at demo speed. A rig that only works on the second try is not ready.

Check that the numbers on the index card are the real numbers from your own measurements this sprint, not guesses. Also check that you can explain in one sentence why the rig needs less force than lifting by hand.
checklist: The rig lifts the chosen load smoothly, tested twice before the family sees it
The index card shows the straight-lift force and the rig's force, both real numbers
I can say in one sentence which trade the rig uses and why it works
The demo runs start to finish without needing to stop and fix something

steps.title: Show the family
steps.body:
Gather the family and run the demo in the order rehearsed: the load, the rig, the lift, then the two numbers on the card. Let someone else try pulling the spring scale on the rig if they want to feel the difference themselves.

End by naming one thing that made the rig hard to get right, since a lever or a gear train that looks simple almost never is on the first attempt.

steps.title: Show it
steps.prompt: A short recording of the rig lifting the load in front of the family, plus a photo of the index card with both numbers written on it
